title: Примирение за чаем  (Making Peace over Tea)

segments.t: That night, Max and Kostya walk into the apartment sporting bruises and a sling, telling Sasha and Nastya that they got into a fistfight because of the girls' endless bickering. Overcome with guilt, Nastya and Sasha immediately apologize to each other and go make tea together.
Да ладно, все с ними в порядке.
Вы из-за нас, что ли, подрались?
Специально для такого случая у нас хранится кое-что.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'Well, how is that?' The grammar packs 'come on' and 'why' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'That does not work either.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'some' and 'not' in a few short words.
Да ладно, все с ними в порядке.
'Come on, they look convincing enough.' Notice how Russian expresses 'yes' and 'order' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Kostya answers right away.
'Kostya, where were you two?' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'be' covers a group or the polite 'you'.
'What happened to you?' Max brings out the contrast between 'what' and 'with' in a few short words.
Вы из-за нас, что ли, подрались?
'Did the two of you get into a fight because of us?' Kostya raises the pitch on 'to fight' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Max answers right away.
'What is the big deal?' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'such a thing' in spoken Russian.
'Well, we had a fight.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'to fight'.
'Everything is fine now anyway.' Max brings out the contrast between 'all' and 'already' in a few short words. Kostya answers right away.
'Let us go have some tea.' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'to drink' in spoken Russian.
'Yes, let us do that.' Notice how Russian expresses 'yes' and 'let's' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'You two get changed while we get everything ready.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'to prepare', turning the action back on the subject. Max answers right away.
Специально для такого случая у нас хранится кое-что.

'We have something saved specially for an occasion like this.' In Russian, the idea of 'on purpose' flows naturally into 'something' without extra filler words. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Да ладно, все с ними в порядке.
Вы из-за нас, что ли, подрались?
Специально для такого случая у нас хранится кое-что.
When you watch Scene 17 of Episode 11, listen out for the exchange around making peace over tea — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
